INGREDIENTS

  • 1.5lbs of strawberries
  • 1 1/2c sugar (should be 2 1/2c)
  • 1 large lemon, juiced

DIRECTIONS

  • On low heat, place strawberries in a pot with lid on for 5 mins.

  • Add sugar and lemon juice, bring to a light boil for 20 mins-25 mins

  • Set aside, cool, and enjoy!

PLEASE NOTE: I cut the sugar content, so I ended up with something quite luquid-ish. Honey, or molasses can be used as a thickening agent should you not wish to use the recommended 2 1/2c of sugar.

YUMMY!

Hello /v/libertarian

I have noticed that there is a quite large amount of users on Voat that want to heavily influnce what mods are allowed in their subreddits or how they must manage them. I've heard proposals about having to hold Mod elections or restricting which posts they can delete.

I get it: bad mods suck. However I do believe that someone who creates a subverse, a community and makes it grow should basically retain his or her right to manage it however they see fit, equaling a subverse to a sort of private property.

Don't get me wrong. I know that Voat is a private website and that it can decide whatever restrictions it wants. However, if we take libertarianism down one level and for the sake of argument we equal it to the government, subverses should be regarded thus as private property and the userbase should not be able to impose restrictions on how someone should manage their own private property.

Am I taking this too far? Is it ok that an increasing amount of users want to restrict what mods can do and what they can't? I mean, if you don't like a subverse it's as easy as creating your own or finding an alternative which, to me, is how it should be.
Is Voat community at risk of becoming too inverventionist?

I think you are "taking this too far," or rather using a bad analogy. Voat administration isn't anything like a government. I agree with you about how it should be run, but the way to argue our case against the "mod elections" advocates is not to use and analogy that doesn't really fit, but to think harder about our real reasons for opposing them. What would voat be like if they get their way? Why would that be bad?

One point that occurs to me is that small communities could get taken over by a kind of super-brigading (people who hated the sub would subscribe to vote out the mods).
Thank you for your reply. It certainly isn't a good analogy, but I hope that my point still stands. In my opinion the userbase wants to meddle too much with the way mods run their subverses.

the userbase should not be able to impose restrictions on how someone should manage their own private property.

The userbase is not "imposing" restrictions. The userbase is negotiating operating practices. All free market transactions are two way streets. The negotiations could either result in a compromise all parties are happy with, or they can break down and both parties go their separate ways.

Yes, that's something I fully understand. However, from the current proposals it seems that people want mods to act a certain way or otherwise threaten with having @atko impose the new rules by which they'll have to abide.

If users and mods don't get along, then everybody goes the separate ways. That's how I think it should be. What in my opinion is not acceptable is to say "Let's make sitewide rule to force mods to act this way". That is clearly an imposition.
It's @atko decision. It's his site. If he feels that being less restrictive than reddit will give him a market advantage then he should be free to do that.
